prompts.title: Recent form: wins, draws and losses
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical frame, roughly 8 seconds total: editorial opening about 5 seconds, statistical block about 3 seconds. Keep the lower quarter reserved for the permanent yellow subtitle band; nothing important may enter it.

Editorial variant — 'Forma en movimiento' (kinetic typography, rhythmic emphasis). Charcoal #101412 background with fine vertical grain. Spanish words 'VICTORIAS', 'EMPATES' and 'DERROTAS' punch in one at a time as oversized condensed capitals in warm white #edf0e6, each snapping on a beat with a small scale overshoot, then settling into a stacked column. A lime #c5ed74 rule sweeps horizontally under each word as it lands. The Spanish team names 'Villarreal CF' and 'SSC Napoli' slide in from opposite edges at mid-height, cross like two runners, and lock into a split composition. A slate #8ca6bf texture band pulses with the rhythm. Camera: continuous slow push-in, ending tighter on the word 'FORMA' as the single focal point. Exit: the letters lift and dissolve. Transition: a beat-synced hard cut into the statistical variant.

Statistical variant — 'Forma reciente'. Spanish heading 'Forma reciente' top-left in warm white with a smaller slate sub-line naming the competition. Two groups of three vertical count bars (grouped count bars), one group per team, ordered wins, draws, losses, all in the same unit of matches. Bars: lime #c5ed74 for 'Villarreal CF', slate #8ca6bf for 'SSC Napoli', with a narrow gap inside each group and a wider gutter between groups. One shared vertical scale with a warm white tick ladder and a Spanish unit label, 'partidos', runs up the left edge; a single warm white zero baseline is shared by every bar. Values sit above their bars: {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Above each group a small Spanish sample annotation shows {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos and flags unequal samples if the renderer reports a difference; a 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' source line sits just above the subtitle band. Entry: bars grow from the zero baseline in a staggered cadence; emphasis: a lime pulse on the leading bar of each group near the two-thirds mark. Camera locked off with a breath of parallax. Exit: bars collapse to the baseline and a soft white flash carries the transition out.

prompts.title: Goals for and against in the recent sample
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical frame, about 9 seconds: editorial opening roughly 5.5 seconds, statistical block roughly 3.5 seconds. The lower quarter stays clear for the permanent yellow subtitles; the pitch artwork stops above that band.

Editorial variant — 'Ruta del balón' (illustrative football pitch and ball path). A top-down pitch drawn in thin warm white #edf0e6 lines on charcoal #101412, with a slate #8ca6bf midline and a lime #c5ed74 centre circle. Spanish heading 'GOLES' in condensed capitals sits in the upper third. A single lime ball travels a curved path from the defensive third into the final third, leaving a short trailing glow; as it reaches the edge of the box the near half of the pitch flashes warm white, then a second ball travels the opposite way along a slate path toward the other goal. Team names 'Villarreal CF' and 'SSC Napoli' anchor at the two ends in warm white, each with a small generic Spanish caption, 'A favor' and 'En contra'. No axes, no numbers, no invented match events — purely illustrative movement. Camera: gentle top-down drift with a slight zoom toward the goalmouth. Emphasis: the held pause at the moment of the strike. Exit: the pitch lines retract toward the centre spot and vanish. Transition: a quick lateral wipe along the slate midline.

Statistical variant — 'Goles a favor y en contra'. Paired horizontal bars, two rows per team, on one shared numeric scale. Spanish title 'Goles en los últimos partidos' in warm white; a single scale labelled 'goles' in Spanish runs across the top with warm white ticks and one thin zero rule. Values are labelled at the end of each bar: {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for 'Villarreal CF', {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for 'SSC Napoli', each carrying the Spanish unit 'goles'. A slate annotation shows the sample behind each pair, {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos, with the word 'muestra', plus a 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' source line above the subtitle band. Forwards bars are lime #c5ed74, against bars slate #8ca6bf. Entry: bars sweep in from the left with a staggered cadence; the difference inside each pair is underlined by a warm white bracket. Emphasis: the widest gap receives a slow lime pulse, whatever the renderer resolves it to be. Camera locked. Exit: bars retract to zero and fade into the transition.

prompts.title: Clean sheets as raw counts against their sample
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical frame, about 7 seconds: editorial shield block roughly 4.5 seconds, statistical count comparison roughly 2.5 seconds. The lower quarter stays clear for the permanent yellow subtitles.

Editorial variant — 'Muro defensivo' (defensive energy, stylised shield). Charcoal #101412 ground with a faint radial vignette. A stylised shield outline in warm white #edf0e6 is drawn stroke by stroke; inside it, slate #8ca6bf wedge shapes stack layer upon layer, and a lime #c5ed74 rim ignites around the shield edge on the final layer. A Spanish heading 'ARCO EN CERO' sits above the shield in condensed capitals. The Spanish team names 'Villarreal CF' and 'SSC Napoli' appear below in warm white, each beside its own shield silhouette; the two silhouettes rotate slowly in opposite directions, then settle. Impact pulses ripple outward on each landing beat and a short slate shockwave travels to the frame edges. No axes, no counts, no invented match events — defensive imagery only. Camera: slow dolly-in ending on the shield rim as the single focal point. Exit: the shield closes and collapses into a thin warm white line. Transition: that line expands into the statistical baseline.

Statistical variant — 'Arcos en cero'. Horizontal count bars, one per team, equal bar height, sitting on a shared zero rule. Spanish heading 'Arcos en cero (muestra reciente)'. Bars render as raw counts only — never converted into rates, averages or shares — with the unit 'partidos' labelled once on the warm white axis. Bar values: {{home.clean}} for 'Villarreal CF' in lime #c5ed74 and {{away.clean}} for 'SSC Napoli' in slate #8ca6bf. Directly beneath each bar a Spanish sample line shows {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos, so each count is read against its own sample. A 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' source line sits above the subtitle band in slate. Entry: bars slide out from the zero rule; emphasis: the longer bar takes a single warm white outline flash, whatever the renderer resolves it to be. Camera locked. Exit: bars retract into the zero rule and fade as the transition to the next scene.

prompts.title: Historical head-to-head counts with total sample
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical frame, about 8 seconds: editorial duel roughly 5 seconds, statistical head-to-head chart roughly 3 seconds. The lower quarter is reserved for the permanent yellow subtitles.

Editorial variant — 'Duelo' (both teams as a visual duel). Charcoal #101412 stage split diagonally into two halves, left tinted lime #c5ed74, right tinted slate #8ca6bf, both at low opacity so the frame stays dark. Two abstract crest silhouettes, one per team, slide in from opposite corners, meet at the centre and clash: on impact a warm white #edf0e6 ring expands and the split line snaps straight. The Spanish labels 'Villarreal CF' and 'SSC Napoli' ride with their silhouettes in warm white capitals, with a Spanish heading 'CARA A CARA' above the impact point. Lime and slate shards scatter after the clash, hold briefly, then settle into a balanced standoff with both silhouettes at the same size to keep the composition neutral. No numbers and no historical claims appear here — it is pure staging. Camera: fast push toward the impact, then a slow settle. Exit: the shards fall out of frame. Transition: the warm white ring becomes the chart frame of the statistical variant.

Statistical variant — 'Cruces previos'. A comparison of historical results: three grouped count bars labelled in Spanish 'Victorias Villarreal CF', 'Empates' and 'Victorias SSC Napoli', all in the shared unit 'partidos'. Values: {{h2h.homeWins}}, {{h2h.draws}} and {{h2h.awayWins}}, with the total sample shown as {{h2h.total}} partidos in a warm white annotation. Colours: lime #c5ed74 for 'Villarreal CF', slate #8ca6bf for 'SSC Napoli', warm white outline for draws. A Spanish caption must state that these figures describe past meetings only and are not a forecast, and a 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' source line sits above the subtitle band. Entry: bars grow from the left along one shared zero baseline; emphasis: a warm white underline sweeps beneath the longest bar, whatever the renderer resolves it to be, without asserting direction in text. Camera locked. Exit: the chart contracts toward the centre and dissolves into the transition.

prompts.title: Synthesis: one grounded statistical tension
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical frame, about 10 seconds: editorial reveal roughly 6 seconds, statistical synthesis roughly 4 seconds. The lower quarter stays clear for the permanent yellow subtitles.

Editorial variant — 'Revelado' (team reveals, narrative emphasis). Charcoal #101412 with a slow drifting lime #c5ed74 haze. The Spanish names 'Villarreal CF' and 'SSC Napoli' are masked by slate #8ca6bf blocks that slide apart to reveal the letters, one team at a time, each reveal accompanied by a warm white #edf0e6 light sweep. A Spanish heading 'DOS PERFILES' sits above, and beneath each reveal a short Spanish phrase drawn from the narration appears in condensed capitals, replacing any numeric claim. The two profiles then hold side by side, each with a faint lime or slate glow, tilting slightly toward each other as the single focal point. No axes and no invented match events. Camera: gentle lateral drift that stops dead on the final hold. Exit: the names fade upward. Transition: a vertical wipe down the centre line into the statistical layout.

Statistical variant — 'Síntesis histórica'. Two labelled comparison pairs, each with its own unit and its own shared scale — never merged into a single scale. Upper pair, unit 'goles': {{home.gf}} for 'Villarreal CF' in lime and {{away.gf}} for 'SSC Napoli' in slate, as paired bars on one shared zero baseline. Lower pair, unit 'partidos': {{home.clean}} for 'Villarreal CF' in lime and {{away.clean}} for 'SSC Napoli' in slate, as paired bars on their own shared zero baseline, shown as raw counts and never converted into rates. Spanish axis labels 'goles' and 'partidos' sit beside their scales, and the sample behind each team is annotated as {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos. No published model estimates exist in this catalog, so everything is presented as history: a Spanish caption reads 'Datos históricos, no una predicción', estimates are not shown and no predictive wording appears. A 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' source line sits above the subtitle band. Entry: the upper pair grows first, then the lower pair; emphasis: a warm white bracket links both pairs to expose the tension between scoring output and defensive solidity, without asserting direction in text. Camera locked. Exit: both pairs retract to their baselines and fade into the transition.
